proposed definition: A family study of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute that recruited families, about half at high risk of coronary heart disease and half selected randomly, from existing study populations at four centres in Forsyth County (North Carolina), Framingham (Massachusetts), Minneapolis (Minnesota) and Salt Lake City (Utah), examining 5,710 participants in 1993–1995, to identify genetic and non-genetic determinants of coronary heart disease, atherosclerosis and their risk factors. label: Colorectal Cancer Genetics & Genomics
current definition: A Spanish colorectal cancer study combining two case-control studies: incident colorectal cancer cases and hospital controls recruited at the University Hospital of Bellvitge, L'Hospitalet de Llobregat (Barcelona), in 1996–1998, and cases and population controls recruited at Bellvitge and the Hospital of León in 2007–2015, genotyped to study the genetics and genomics of colorectal cancer.

evidence quote: CRCGEN combines data of two Spanish case-control studies. The first one, conducted in the University Hospital of Bellvitge, L’Hospitalet del Llobregat, (Barcelona), recruited incident pathology-confirmed CRC cases ( n = 304) and age and sex frequency-matched hospital controls ( n = 293) during the period 1996–1998. The control group was randomly selected among patients without previous CRC admitted to the same hospital during the same period. To avoid selection bias, the criterion of inclusion in the control group was a new diagnosis. The second study was conducted in parallel in the University Hospital of Bellvitge and in the Hospital of León, León, during 2007–2015 and recruited a total of 633 incident CRC cases (313 Bellvitge and 320 León) and 571 population controls (free of CRC, 164 Bellvitge and 407 León).

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank
current definition: A longitudinal hospital-based cohort and biobank of patients of the Montreal Heart Institute, a cardiology hospital enriched for cardiovascular disease, who consented to give a baseline blood sample with medical, nutritional, psychosocial, sociodemographic and lifestyle data, updated through hospital record linkage and four-yearly follow-up interviews, and who are genotyped for genetic and pharmacogenomic studies.

evidence quote: The MHI Biobank is a longitudinal cohort with the aim to recruit 30,000 patients of the MHI for clinical and genetic research ... The Cohort’s database is updated frequently with patients’ medical information from the hospital’s electronic records. A follow-up study questionnaire is administered every four years.
